rationale: The workflow is a Rust CI with repeated runs (CI history shows multiple successful runs) and no existing dependency cache. Cargo re-downloads registry and git dependencies on every run across the build_and_test matrix (ubuntu/windows/macOS). The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (Cache dependency downloads) applies: repeated dependency fetching is measurable, and the cache can be keyed on the runner OS plus Cargo.lock. The measured experiment batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200 reported about 20.4% elapsed savings from adding a dependency cache to a CI workflow, and the pattern reports modest aggregate VM-time reduction. The change adds a single actions/cache@v4 step for ~/.cargo/registry and ~/.cargo/git after checkout and before cargo build in build_and_test. It preserves all build/test coverage (no steps or tests removed), caches only dependency downloads rather than build outputs, and adds no permissions, secrets, privileged actions, publishing/deployment, or new network access beyond the existing GitHub Actions cache service.
